title: HW2 round 1: make six requirement-claiming tests check their requirement
description: First HW2 improvement round. Strategy: give the agent the application's intended behaviour for six areas (PDF metadata, summary request IDs, pinned chat follow-ups, upload Cancel, PDF download hosts and port, search Load more), have it say which existing test claims each one and whether it really checks it, then repair or add tests. Test-only change: no application code is touched. User rulings: test the upload pipeline as it ships with a mocked model and no provider match, counting a bug only if a required field stays empty after that; keep parser-only checks as unit tests, not bug evidence; test Cancel on the client only and log the server case separately. A second batch followed the user's review: the stored-PDF re-read paths, a collapse test that never collapsed, an assertion on a fixture constant, two tests of one gate, and a rebuilt E2E-03.
acceptance_criteria: Given an uploaded PDF, when the pipeline runs with a mocked model and no provider match, then title, authors, year and abstract are asserted against the PDF's printed values, and a field left empty is recorded as a bug.
Given two deliberate summary requests, when both are sent, then their request IDs differ, a new ID starts a new job and a repeated ID replays the first.
Given a chat pinned to a PDF that was removed or replaced, when a follow-up is asked, then a contract-valid answer completes from the pinned PDF.
Given an upload in flight on any Cancel button, when Cancel is pressed, then the transfer is aborted and a late response cannot accept the paper.
Given a redirect to an allowed host on a non-default port, when a PDF is fetched, then it is refused before contacting that host, while the explicit default port is allowed.
Given two provider pages, when the continuation is followed through the client and the API, then the exact cursor or offset is sent and a distinct second page arrives.

Given a refresh of an upload with no provider record, when its stored PDF is read again, then storage failures, DOI ownership, authors, manual values and a paper deleted mid-read behave as specified, and metadata.py lines 328-333, 356-361, 367-368 and 397-398 execute.
Given a PDF with no existing record, when it is uploaded in the browser, then its title, authors, year and abstract come from the PDF.
Given each behaviour above, when the matching production code is faulted in memory, then at least one new or changed test fails.
Given the final tree, when measured as in docs/hw2-baseline.md, then the comparison with the initial suite is recorded, including what did not improve.
verification: Final measurement on 2026-11-08 in the isolated ara-hw2-r1-test project with the settings in docs/hw2-baseline.md; application source identical to b40405b. Ruff passed. Backend with real services: 1281 passed, 3 xfailed in 317.78 s, 8611/9050 lines (95.15%), 2028/2378 branches (85.28%), 13 data sets combined and 35 skipped (initial: 1228 passed, 8584 lines, 2011 branches). Frontend: 772 passed in 94 files, 3186/3322 lines (95.90%), 3474/3968 branches (87.55%), with TypeScript and ESLint passing (initial: 766, 3184 lines, 3474 branches). Playwright on a fresh database: 27 passed in 3.6 min. Infrastructure: 46 OK. Whole Vitest under each fault on the final tree: setOpen(true) 1 failed and 771 passed; upload abort removed 4 failed and 768 passed; fixed summary request_id 1 failed and 771 passed; old invalid chat fixture 2 failed and 770 passed. Earlier targeted faults, each caught: port 7, cursor ignored 3, empty-page cursor 1, route drops cursor 1, chat scope uses active PDF 2, summary request ID ignored 1, values not saved 4, model values not merged 1, parser abstract 4, parser year 4, nine re-read faults, three summary-card faults, XMP authors 1, and four E2E-03 field faults through a changed parser in the real worker. A targeted coverage run confirmed every listed metadata.py line executes. Three strict xfails record ARA-118 (2) and ARA-120 (1). Not improved or worse: frontend branch coverage unchanged, most baseline uncovered paths untouched, backend run 21.32 s slower, the reader's Replace PDF browser path lost. Faults were known in advance and hand-picked, so no mutation score is claimed. Live providers were not used. Details in docs/hw2-round-1.md.
